Article.ArticleTitle: Use of the SAMe-TT2R2 score to predict anticoagulation control in atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism patients treated with vitamin K antagonists: A review.

Abstract.AbstractText: Identifying patients who are likely to achieve and maintain a therapeutic international normalized ratio when prescribed a vitamin K antagonist for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) is challenging. The SAMe-TT2R2 score was developed on the basis of common clinical factors that can highlight patients who may be unable to achieve and maintain good anticoagulation control and for whom a "trial of warfarin" would be inadvisable. This review summarizes the main published prospective and retrospective studies that have validated the SAMe-TT2R2 score in AF and VTE patients treated with a vitamin K antagonist and how the SAMe-TT2R2 score could aid clinical decision making; 19 studies were included. Taken together, validation studies suggest that the SAMe-TT2R2 score is able to predict good or poor anticoagulation control in AF and VTE patients, although data on VTE patients are limited (3 studies). The available evidence suggests that the SAMe-TT2R2 score may be a useful tool to aid clinical decision making for oral anticoagulants in AF and VTE patients.
